# Audit: final `-TE`

**Status:** completed first-pass audit of the six exact-extension pairs generated by the frozen v0.2 blind ranking.  
**Blind rank:** suffix #4 / 116.  
**Davis 2026:** independently identifies `-TE` as one of four likely Linear A suffixes.  
**Result:** strong distributional/scholarly suffix candidate, but **0 new Tier-A exact pairs** from the six automatically generated pairs; two formal survivors remain candidate/reclassified cases.

## Why `-TE` was audited

The blind v0.2 pipeline ranked `TE` fourth among final signs before Brent Davis's six affix identities were known. After unblinding, Davis independently identified `-TE` as one of his four suffix candidates. This makes `TE` a high-value agreement case.

The automatic whole-word comparison generated:

1. `DU-RI ~ DU-RI-TE`
2. `SI-RU ~ SI-RU-TE`
3. `KU-NI ~ KU-NI-TE`
4. `I-JA ~ I-JA-TE`
5. `A-DI-KI-TE ~ A-DI-KI-TE-TE`
6. `A-TA-NA ~ A-TA-NA-TE`

Each was checked against a damage-aware concordance and contextual/scholarly evidence.

## Pair-by-pair adjudication

### 1. `DU-RI ~ DU-RI-TE` — rejected as an exact pair

The damage-aware concordance preserves both forms with an insecure left boundary:

- `] du-ri`
- `] du-ri-te`

The cleaned computational corpus therefore overstates both as complete words. Because the material preceding `DU-` is unknown, this cannot serve as a secure whole-word `X ~ X-TE` pair.

**Adjudication:** rejected for benchmark exact-pair evidence.

### 2. `SI-RU ~ SI-RU-TE` — formal survivor, lexical identity unresolved

Both forms have secure complete attestations:

- `SI-RU` — HT 55a.2, administrative tablet;
- `SI-RU-TE` — securely complete on IO Za 2.2 and KO Za 1c-d, with additional damaged/restored ritual attestations.

The problem is contextual. `SI-RU-TE` is a highly recurrent terminal element of the Linear A libation formula, whereas the only secure bare `SI-RU` is an administrative occurrence at Haghia Triada. The formal relationship is real, but the genre mismatch is severe enough that common lexical identity cannot simply be assumed.

Rose Thomas (2020) treats `SI-RU-TE` as part of the structured libation formula rather than deriving it from an independently established `SI-RU` stem. Recent work on the formula likewise treats `SI-RU-TE` as a recurrent sign group.

**Adjudication:** Tier B / reclassified formal comparison. It supports investigation of `-TE` but is not a Tier-A inflectional pair.

### 3. `KU-NI ~ KU-NI-TE` — rejected as an exact pair

The damage-aware concordance records the supposed base only as:

- `] ku-ni [`

while `KU-NI-TE` is complete at KH 92.1.

The cleaned corpus flattened the damaged base into `KU-NI`, manufacturing a whole-word extension pair.

`KU-NI-TE` has also been compared with Linear B `ku-ni-ta` as a personal name, which independently raises an onomastic explanation for the full form.

**Adjudication:** rejected for exact-pair evidence.

### 4. `I-JA ~ I-JA-TE` — secure forms, but no demonstrated derivation

Both forms are complete:

- `I-JA` — CR(?) Zf 1;
- `I-JA-TE` — PH Zb 4.

They occur on different objects/sites and no repeated administrative role currently links them. The identical `i-ja-te` sequence also occurs in Linear B, but Steele and Meißner explicitly caution that the Linear B Greek word and Linear A `I-JA-TE` need not be the same lexical item. Thus cross-script resemblance cannot establish the internal Linear A derivation either.

**Adjudication:** Tier C / comparison-only. Formally compatible with final `-TE`, but lexical identity of `I-JA` and `I-JA-TE` remains unproven.

### 5. `A-DI-KI-TE ~ A-DI-KI-TE-TE` — rejected as a mechanical exact pair; independently important to scholarship

The damage-aware concordance gives:

- `a-di-ki-te [` — PK Za 12.b;
- `a-di-ki-te-te [` and longer ritual forms such as `a-di-ki-te-te-du-...-re`.

The bare computational form therefore does not have a secure right word boundary. It cannot be counted as a mechanically proven `X ~ X-TE` pair.

However, this family is independently important. Miguel Valério (2007/2008) argued from the ritual expression `j/a-di-ki-te-te ... du-pu2-re` for a morphological analysis involving Dikte. Peter Schrijver (2024/2025) accepts the possibility that `a-di-ki-te-te` contains a suffix but cautions that the exact function is not established. This is **scholarly morphological evidence separate from our exact-pair benchmark**.

**Adjudication:** rejected as an automatic minimal pair; retained as literature-supported morphology evidence.

### 6. `A-TA-NA ~ A-TA-NA-TE` — rejected as an exact pair

The apparent base is actually preserved as:

- `a-ta-na-[•]` — ZA 9.4-5

whereas `A-TA-NA-TE` is complete at ZA 10a.2. The corpus again flattened a damaged continuation into a bare form.

ZA 10 contains `TA-NA-TE` and `A-TA-NA-TE`, which remains important for the independent `A-` prefix question, but it does **not** establish `A-TA-NA ~ A-TA-NA-TE`.

**Adjudication:** rejected for exact `-TE` evidence.

## External comparison: `AU-RE ~ AU-RE-TE`

Peter Schrijver discusses an additional pair not recovered by our mechanical exact-pair generator: `AU-RE ~ AU-RE-TE`, interpreting the latter as a suffixed form while explicitly leaving the function of `-TE` open. This is valuable because it demonstrates that the six corpus-generated exact pairs are not the complete evidentiary universe for `-TE`.

This comparison should receive a dedicated epigraphic audit before benchmark promotion.

## Result

The six automatic pairs resolve as:

| automatic pair | result |
|---|---|
| `DU-RI ~ DU-RI-TE` | rejected: left boundary damaged |
| `SI-RU ~ SI-RU-TE` | formal survivor; severe genre/formula mismatch |
| `KU-NI ~ KU-NI-TE` | rejected: base fragmentary |
| `I-JA ~ I-JA-TE` | comparison-only; lexical identity unproven |
| `A-DI-KI-TE ~ A-DI-KI-TE-TE` | rejected as mechanical pair; independent scholarly morphology argument survives |
| `A-TA-NA ~ A-TA-NA-TE` | rejected: base fragmentary |

Thus the blind exact-pair bonus substantially overestimated the clean pair support for `TE`, even though `TE` remains a strong boundary-enriched sign and independently matches Davis's suffix set.

## Interpretation

The `TE` audit reinforces the distinction first exposed by `RO`:

> **boundary enrichment, exact stem alternation, and grammatical function are three different evidentiary questions.**

A final sign may be genuinely morphological even when a cleaned corpus invents many of the apparent minimal pairs supporting it. Conversely, literature-based or contextual evidence can support morphology that a strict exact-pair detector misses.

The next scoring pipeline should therefore separate:

1. pure edge-distribution evidence;
2. damage-aware exact-pair evidence;
3. onomastic/formulaic concentration;
4. contextual grammatical evidence.

## Sources used in this audit

- Damage-aware Linear A concordance, Ancient Scripts Study / LinA, entries under `DU`, `SI`, `KU`, `I`, and `A` (secondary concordance; important claims should ultimately be checked against GORILA/SigLA).
- Miguel Valério, “'Diktaian Master': A Minoan Predecessor of Diktaian Zeus in Linear A?”, *Kadmos* 46 (2007/2008).
- Peter Schrijver, “Talking Neolithic: The Case for Hatto-Minoan,” discussion of `AU-RE-TE` and `-TE`.
- Rose Thomas, “Some reflections on morphology in the language of the Linear A libation formula,” *Kadmos* 59 (2020).
- Philippa M. Steele and Torsten Meißner, discussion of Linear A / Linear B lexical comparisons and the caution surrounding `I-JA-TE`.

## Benchmark consequence

No new Tier-A `-TE` minimal pair is promoted from the six automatic candidates. The negative rows should nevertheless be added to `data/morphology-benchmark.csv`, because they are valuable labeled false positives for future morphology algorithms.
